clue.text: Let's Dance, David's non-US no.1 single

definitions.text: Let's Dance, David's non-US no.1 single

parts.words: Let's Dance, David's non-US no.1 single
parts.note: a cryptic hint at a David Bowie single whose title pairs what is heard with what is seen, as at a dance

explanation.surface: A pop fan recalling which of David Bowie's singles topped charts outside America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a puzzle-wide nod to Bowie: it points at one of his singles rather than building it from pieces. 'Let's Dance' was itself a Bowie hit, which sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1977 Bowie single from the album Low carries this title, naming audio and picture together.

clue.text: Press 5's mouth here?

definitions.meaning: to press someone is to force them into service, especially as a sailor kidnapped for a crew
5 is the great Chinese river, which reaches the sea beside this port city

explanation.surface: A journalist asking where a river's mouth lies, as if press reporters gathered there.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghaiing is the old practice of drugging men onto ships; the city also sits at the river's estuary.

clue.text: Make the rounds with jutting jaw

indicators.note: make here means fashion something new out of these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer or doctor doing the rounds with a pugnacious, jutting jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make the rounds' reads as a phrase meaning do a circuit, but 'Make' signals rearranging the letters of THE ROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An undershot jaw has the lower jaw projecting beyond the upper, giving a jutting chin.

clue.text: As a tear appears at first, David — rest in peace

definitions.text: As a tear appears at first, David — rest in peace

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the name that follows

parts.note: RIP is the standard abbreviation for rest in peace on gravestones

explanation.surface: A mourner's farewell to David Bowie, a tear forming as they say rest in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer: a tear first shows as a single falling drop of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear first appears as a single falling bead of liquid, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Move those 27, with the wave of a magic wand!

definitions.text: with the wave of a magic wand!

indicators.note: move tells us to shift these letters around into a new order

parts.note: 27 across is a heap for burning, a funeral pile

explanation.surface: A conjuror ordering some objects to move by waving a wand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' signals rearranging THOSE together with PYRE, the answer to 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stage magician's exclamation at the moment a trick is completed by a wave of the wand.

clue.text: Oh well; I gather dry grass with this tool

indicators.note: I gather can mean I hear, so it signals a word judged by its sound

parts.note: dry grass is hay, and the tool for working it is a hoe

explanation.surface: A resigned farmhand sighing 'oh well' while raking hay with a hoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gather' here means I hear: HAY HOE sounds like the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses mild weariness or resignation, much like a sighed 'oh well'.

clue.text: A net Ziggy regularly cast here (together with China Girl)?

indicators.note: a net is cast when thrown, and cast also means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
regularly takes every other letter of the word Ziggy

explanation.surface: Ziggy Stardust fishing with a net in a Chinese river, alongside Bowie's China Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ZGY from Ziggy; 'cast' then rearranges these with A NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of China is where a net would be cast in the scene, the place China Girl belongs.

clue.text: Genre leading to suicide, according to Bowie

definitions.meaning: a style of popular music from the 1950s

definitions.text: leading to suicide, according to Bowie
definitions.meaning: Bowie's song ... Suicide closes the Ziggy Stardust album, so this phrase precedes suicide in that title

explanation.surface: A music critic claiming that, by Bowie's account, one style of music drives people to suicide.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s style of popular music is a genre, and it is also the opening of a Bowie song title.

clue.text: Single actor welcomes unusual sex

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one part goes inside the actor's name

parts.note: Kevin Spacey is an American actor
unusual means odd
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A gossip item about an unmarried actor who enjoys unusual sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a marital status but is the definition: a record. 'welcomes' puts the inner pieces inside the actor Kevin Spacey's surname; 'it' is a coy word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowie's 1969 single about Major Tom carries this title, so it is an example of a single.

clue.text: See 7
See 1
Leafy green Somerset town

definitions.meaning: a leaf vegetable related to beet
a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Describing a pleasant, tree-lined town in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is a leafy green beet, and a small town of the same name lies in Somerset.

clue.text: Boast about clothes

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for boast is read backwards

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Someone showing off about their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals reading BRAG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or dress, often distinctive attire.

clue.text: Pallid, like the lean nobleman of the artist's imagination?

definitions.text: like the lean nobleman of the artist's imagination?
definitions.meaning: Bowie's 1970s stage persona was the Thin ... Duke, a lean nobleman he invented

explanation.surface: Describing a pale, thin aristocrat from a painter's imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and lacking colour; the word is also the middle of Bowie's Thin White Duke persona.

clue.text: Despatched with Absolute Beginners missing

indicators.note: the clue reads as the answer with the initials added making the word for away, so they are taken off that word

parts.note: missing means absent, not present
the beginners of Absolute Beginners are its first letters, A and B

explanation.surface: Something sent off without the Bowie song Absolute Beginners included.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as: the answer with AB, the first letters of Absolute Beginners, makes ABSENT, meaning missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Despatched means posted or sent off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 16
See 6
Single American Airlines hostess he's corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or garbled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: AA is the abbreviation for the airline American Airlines

explanation.surface: An unmarried American Airlines flight attendant, the clue implies, has been led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' is the record, not marital status. 'corrupted' rearranges AA, HOSTESS and HE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowie's 1980 single, a sequel to the Major Tom story, is an example of a single.

clue.text: As seen by Major Tom, a cabaret singer

parts.note: Major Tom, the astronaut of Space Oddity, looks back and sees our planet, which is blue

explanation.surface: Major Tom spotting a cabaret singer from his capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: In Space Oddity Major Tom sings that 'planet Earth is blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eartha Kitt was a famous American cabaret singer and actress.

clue.text: From America, fine album

definitions.meaning: an American slang expression meaning fine or satisfactory
Bowie's 1971 album containing Changes and Life on Mars?

explanation.surface: Praising a good record that comes from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is American slang for fine or all right, and is also the title of a Bowie album.

clue.text: Carries out tests on female donkeys?

definitions.meaning: a jocular feminine of asses, formed like lionesses from lions

explanation.surface: A vet examining some she-donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to judge by testing; the word also splits as a mock feminine plural of donkeys.

clue.text: Kate's run round with her kit off!

definitions.text: Kate's run round with her kit off!

indicators.note: round suggests turning the letters about, rearranging them

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A woman named Kate dashing around naked, as at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' shuffles KATE'S with R, the abbreviation for run; the whole clue also describes the act.
explanation.definitionFit: To run about naked in public, as at a sports match, is the classic act of this name.

clue.text: Dagger gutted Helen, a deity

parts.note: a kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade

indicators.note: gutted means with the insides removed, so only the outside letters of the name stay

explanation.surface: A violent picture of Helen stabbed by a dagger, then a nod to a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the inside of HELEN, leaving HN.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a major Hindu god, worshipped as an avatar of Vishnu.

clue.text: Accountant provides support at the beginning of the month

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
to lend support is to provide it, so lends fits

explanation.surface: An accountant helping someone out financially at the start of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant, a common abbreviation in British puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the calends were the first day of each month.

clue.text: Remixes album track

definitions.meaning: alters or reworks, as a remix alters a recording
the opening song on Bowie's Hunky Dory album

explanation.surface: Describing new versions of a song from an LP.
explanation.definitionFit: To remix is to alter; Bowie's song on Hunky Dory carries the same title.

clue.text: South Africa supporting railway company, at first cold

indicators.note: at first places the company abbreviation at the very start
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath the other pieces

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A railway company with South African backing, beginning to feel cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts ZA below CO and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Coryza is the medical term for a head cold, inflammation of the nasal membranes.

clue.text: In Cincinnati, Bowie returned for tribute

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so those concealed letters are read in reverse
In shows the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: Bowie making a return visit to Cincinnati to pay tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: TIBO sits inside 'Cincinnati, Bowie'; 'returned' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary notice is a written tribute to someone who has died.

clue.text: Fashionable American-English prevailing

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Stylish American English being the dominant form of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Something currently employed or current is prevailing at the moment.

clue.text: Some relief in albums like Blackstar

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fans finding comfort in Bowie's records, like his last one, Blackstar.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackstar was released two days before Bowie died in January 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackstar was Bowie's last album, released just before his death.

clue.text: A heap of material from old record company with radical content

indicators.note: content here means contents, what is held inside

parts.note: Pye was a British record label of the 1950s to 1970s
R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: Describing a stockpile of products from a defunct label with extreme content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as contented but means held inside: R goes into PYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyre is a heap of wood or other combustible material, for burning a body.

clue.text: Citrus fruit imported by Italian region, according to natives

indicators.note: imported by means held inside, so only the interior of the regional name is used

parts.note: Puglia is the Italian name for Apulia, the heel of Italy

explanation.surface: A fruit being shipped in by a region of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside PUGLIA, the region's own name for Apulia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican cross between grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Disown bits of Golden Years

indicators.note: bits of says the answer is a stretch of letters from inside these words

explanation.surface: Rejecting fragments of Bowie's song Golden Years.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny someone is to disown or repudiate them.

clue.text: Single stock from a mom and pop store?

definitions.meaning: a record released on its own; this was Bowie's 1975 hit

definitions.text: stock from a mom and pop store?
definitions.meaning: stock as offspring: the children of American moms and pops

explanation.surface: One item of goods from a small family-run American shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowie's 1975 single has this title, and the phrase fits the offspring of US parents.

clue.text: Refugees embrace Sharon, returning after university

indicators.note: after places the turned surname following the university letter

parts.note: to embrace is to hug

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the surname is read backwards

parts.note: Sharon Stone is an American actress

explanation.surface: Refugees welcoming someone called Sharon on her return from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharon' leads to the actress Sharon Stone; 'returning' gives ENOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were French Protestants who fled persecution as refugees in the 1600s.

clue.text: See 30
Ma's playthings?

parts.note: Ma is the cellist Yo-Yo Ma, so his toys would be named after his first name

explanation.walkthrough: Ma looks like mother, but it is the cellist Yo-Yo Ma.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys on a string that spin up and down, and also playfully the possessions of the cellist.
